A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftKI research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix B report original UCI and MD22 regression results, timing measurements, and loss, noise, solver, and interpolation-point analyses.

after.justification: Sections 5 and Appendices B–C report original regression and predictive NLL results, Ricker wavelet experiments, and analyses of learned interpolation points.

M1.justification: v2 adds learnable interpolation temperatures, including per-dimension temperatures. Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1 replace pseudoloss-only optimization with an exact MLL objective that falls back to Hutchinson’s pseudoloss. Algorithm 1 also replaces the fixed-noise requirement with a learnable noise parameter.

E1.justification: The twelve UCI datasets and seven MD22 molecular datasets remain. v2 adds a synthetic Ricker wavelet regression scenario; the additional SKI comparisons and projection analyses otherwise use retained datasets.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated SKI baseline in the Ricker experiment and comparisons against Exact GP, SKIP, and Simplex-SKI in Table 7. Table 7 explicitly imports those baseline scores from Kapoor et al. (2021). SGPR and SVGP remain the main benchmark comparators, while the timing comparison newly includes SGPR.

E3.justification: The benchmark kernel changes from RBF to Matérn 3/2, and MD22 training increases from 50 to 200 epochs. Predictive NLL and new Ricker and SKI-comparison protocols are added. The UCI 90/10 split remains, but Appendix C.3’s new comparison lists inconsistent split fractions: 4/9, 2/9, and 4/9.

E4.justification: v2 adds Ricker reconstruction and probe-count studies, PCA/UMAP analyses of point placement, and lengthscale/temperature histograms. It revises the loss, posterior-solver, and interpolation-point-count analyses. v1’s fixed-versus-learned-noise study and separate pseudoloss-solver comparison on Pol are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark averages across three seeds with ± summaries. No changed repeated-run practice, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Benchmark RMSE and timing results are extensively replaced, and NLL and SKI-family comparison results are added. SoftKI’s bike RMSE changes from 0.204 to 0.062, while its MD22 RMSE lead changes from seven molecules to five. These are results under revised settings, not established same-setting gains. Figure 5’s replacement solver curves also converge much more closely than in v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds temperature-dependent interpolation and stabilized-MLL definitions and revises the pseudoloss expressions and derivatives. It corrects the Cholesky-factor orientation and removes an extra factor from the posterior covariance expression. Appendix A adds a covariance-inference derivation while retaining the two existing inversion lemmas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow claims of superior or outperforming accuracy to competitive performance, including on molecular data. v2 also makes the structural difference between learned interpolation points and variational inducing points a central contribution.

C2.justification: v1’s explanation favoring fixed noise is removed. v2 adds interpretations connecting point placement to inducing-variable priors, NLL to noise and model complexity, and temperature to dimensional relevance. It attributes some degradation with additional interpolation points to overfitting, whereas v1 explicitly described that behavior as unexplained.

D1.justification: v2 documents Ricker sample counts, initialization, optimizer/scheduler settings, and the lengthscale cap. Hardware details are retained but relocated. v1’s explicit code-access link is omitted from v2; this establishes a documentation loss, not that the repository disappeared.

R1.justification: v2 adds VNNGP discussion and supporting citations for ARD, numerical GP approximations, UMAP, and Ricker wavelets, while dropping Gibbs and MacKay (1996). The existing SGPR/SKI context remains, with a sharper distinction between interpolation and variational inducing points.

P1.justification: The framing, background, method exposition, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Section 5.3 changes from noise behavior to learned-point analysis, hardware and timing move into the appendix, and supplementary material is reorganized into separate algorithmic-choice and additional-experiment sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redrawn with interpolation-weight displays; earlier kernel/noise heatmaps disappear; and Ricker, PCA, UMAP, and histogram figures are added. Solver and point-count plots are redrawn, and tables are expanded and reorganized for NLL, timing, and SKI comparisons.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful probabilistic evaluation and geometric analyses, corrects inference algebra, and moderates superiority claims. However, Section 5.1’s training-objective description conflicts with Algorithm 1 and Appendix B.1, the new SKI comparison has inconsistent split fractions, and Figure 5’s closely converging solvers do not support the retained claim that only QR is stable. These conflicts affect validation of the revised method, leaving the net quality improvement uncertain.
